title: 江南曲（嫁得瞿塘贾）
author: 李益
intro: A merchant’s wife complains, half joking and half in tears: the tide at least comes back on time — she should have married a boy who rides the waves.
analysis: 这首诗用一个商人妻子的口吻说话。她嫁给了在长江瞿塘峡一带做生意的商人，丈夫总是说好哪天回来，却一天又一天地失约。后两句是一句“气话”：早知道潮水涨落那么守时，还不如嫁给在潮水里玩耍的弄潮儿！潮水“有信”（按时来），丈夫却“无信”，一个巧妙的对比，把等待的委屈、埋怨和思念都说出来了。这种话说得天真、直率，像民歌一样，所以特别动人。诗人是男性，却把女子的心思写得很真实，这类诗叫“闺怨诗”，是唐诗里常见的题材。
analysisEn: The poem speaks in the voice of a merchant’s wife. Her husband trades along the Qutang Gorge on the Yangtze, and day after day he misses the date he promised to come home. The last two lines are what she blurts out in frustration: “If I had known the tide keeps its word, I’d have married a boy who plays in the tide!” The wordplay is the heart of the poem. 信 means both “on time, regular” and “keeping one’s word”: the tide comes back faithfully, her husband doesn’t. In one clever comparison she says everything — hurt, complaint and longing all at once. Of course she doesn’t really mean it; it is the kind of thing people say when they miss someone. The tone is naive and direct, like a folk song, and that is what makes it so touching. Many Tang poems were written by men in a waiting woman’s voice; this kind of poem is called a “boudoir lament” (闺怨诗).
background: Li Yi (746–829) was a Tang poet famous above all for his frontier quatrains, which were set to music in his own lifetime. “Southern Song” was an old folk-song title, and he wrote this in the plain style of southern love songs.
pronunciation: 瞿塘 qú táng；贾 gǔ（商人，不读姓氏的 jiǎ）；朝朝 zhāo zhāo（天天，不读 cháo）；妾 qiè；嫁与 yǔ；弄潮 nòng。机器朗读“贾”“朝朝”易读错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行本（《唐诗三百首》），各本文字基本一致。

lines.en: I married a trader on the Qutang Gorge,

lines.lit: day after day he misses my appointed date.
lines.en: and every day he breaks the day he promised me.

lines.lit: Had I known the tide keeps its word,
lines.en: If I had known the tide always comes back on time,

lines.lit: I would have married a tide-playing boy.
lines.en: I’d have married a boy who rides the waves.

words.en: the Qutang Gorge, first of the Yangtze’s Three Gorges
words.note: 今重庆奉节附近，现代仍叫瞿塘峡。
古义读 gǔ；现代汉语说“商人”，“商贾”还用。
“朝”读 zhāo，是早晨；现代汉语说“天天”。

words.en: I (a humble word used by a woman for herself)
words.note: 古代女子自称，现代汉语不用；今天的“妾”指小老婆。

words.en: being on time; keeping one’s word
words.note: 现代汉语“守信”“信用”；“潮信”指潮水按时涨落。

words.en: a young man who plays in the tidal waves
words.note: 现代汉语比喻敢于冒险、走在潮流前面的人，如“时代的弄潮儿”。

imagery.name: 长江
imagery.zh: 丈夫在瞿塘峡一带经商，长江的路又远又险，隔开了夫妻。
imagery.en: The husband trades in the Yangtze gorges — a long, dangerous river road that keeps husband and wife apart.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 潮水涨落有定时，和不守约的丈夫形成对比，说出妻子的委屈。
imagery.en: The tide rises and falls on schedule — the perfect contrast with a husband who never returns when he says he will.
